title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
prompt:
Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the k-th largest element in the array. Note that it is the k-th largest element in sorted order, not the k-th distinct element.

You must solve this without sorting the entire array, i.e. in better than O(n log n) average time.

examples.explanation: With a single-element array and k=1, the only element is trivially both the largest and the answer.

hints: A full sort works but costs O(n log n) — the problem asks for something better on average.
Maintain a min-heap of size k over the elements seen so far; the heap top is always the k-th largest of everything processed.
Alternatively, Quickselect (partition-based selection, like a truncated quicksort) finds the k-th largest in O(n) average time by only recursing into the partition that must contain the answer.

solution.approach: Use Quickselect: pick a pivot, partition the array so elements greater than the pivot come before it and elements less come after (partitioning for descending order), then check which side the k-th largest position falls into and recurse only into that side, discarding the other half entirely. Because only one partition is ever explored, the expected work is O(n) + O(n/2) + O(n/4) + ... = O(n), versus O(n log n) for sorting the whole array.
solution.spaceComplexity: O(1) extra (in-place partitioning, aside from recursion stack)
